correctness.rationale: For \(k=\alpha+1\) and \(h=n+1\), the two generators (cycle, counter shift \(1\)) and (transposition, counter shift \(0\)) project onto \(S_k\). The words \(a^k\) and \((ab)^{k-1}\) project to the identity but shift the counter by the coprime residues \(k\) and \(k-1\), yielding the full product \(S_k\times\mathbb Z/h\mathbb Z\). The source and auxiliary automata are reachable and pairwise distinguishable with \(m\) and \(n\) final states. Accepted auxiliary words project to the point stabilizer of \(k\), so the quotient final set is \([k-1]\) and its minimal DFA has \(\alpha\) final states. Rauch--Holzer Corollary 32 provides all smaller \(\alpha\), while nonemptiness excludes zero; 75 finite tests and independent DFA refinements matched.

value.rationale: Alphabet size is an intrinsic resource in the unary-to-nonunary right-quotient spectrum problem. The known high-range result uses three letters and proves existence over unspecified finite alphabets, leaving the sharp fixed-alphabet threshold unresolved. A coprime-relations construction supplies an exact and nontrivial two-letter realization, and the finite unary interval proves that two is best possible. This is a structurally motivated complete alphabet-threshold determination, not merely a routine parameter increment or a repetition of the output spectrum.
